_what: Rigma on a Runpod GPU pod — the template/pod definition, as a field-by-field spec. The field NAMES and shapes here are the live ones, read from Runpod's own catalog on 2026-10-07 (see _schema_provenance); the VALUES are this deployment's. The README gives the commands; this file is the canonical list of what they must carry.

_schema_provenance.verified_from_the_catalog: GET https://api.runpod.io/v2/catalog/templates with the account's own key returned 14 stock templates whose records use exactly these fields: allowedCudaVersions, args, category, disk, env, id, image, mounts, name, ports, public, registry, serverless, startJupyter, startSsh. The shape below is copied from 'Runpod Pytorch 2.4.0' (id runpod-torch-v240), which uses EXACTLY the base image this Dockerfile pins (runpod/pytorch:2.4.0-py3.11-cuda12.4.1-devel-ubuntu22.04) — so disk=20, mounts.persistent={path:/workspace,size:20}, ports=[8888/http,22/tcp], env={} and startSsh/startJupyter=true are the vendor's own values for this base, not inferences.
_schema_provenance.verified_from_a_cpu_template: 'Runpod Ubuntu 24.04' (id runpod-ubuntu-2404, image runpod/base:1.0.2-ubuntu2404, category CPU) declares ports ["8888/http","22/tcp"], disk 10, env {}, startJupyter true, startSsh true — i.e. the Ubuntu templates and the GPU templates agree on the port/ssh/jupyter shape, which is what this template follows.
_schema_provenance.ports_shape: `ports` is an ARRAY of "<port>/<proto>" strings in the GPU/Ubuntu records, but a bare STRING in 'Network storage file browser' ("80/http"), so both are accepted. /http means Runpod's HTTP proxy fronts that port.
_schema_provenance.mounts_shape: Only `persistent` is ACCEPTED. The catalog showed {"persistent":{"path":"/workspace","size":20}}, and POSTing any `network` key under `mounts` to POST /v2/templates returns 422 `$.mounts: additional properties 'network' not allowed` — both the object form {"volumeMountPath":"/workspace"} and the array form [{"volumeId":"..."}] taken from the runpod-migrate reference were refused with that same message. So `mounts.network` is a POD-creation field (--network-volume-id + --volume-mount-path /workspace), not a template field, and it is no longer declared below.
_schema_provenance.env_is_empty_on_every_stock_template: All 14 stock templates have env {} — including every NVIDIA one. So NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES is NOT set by the platform's own templates; whether the host injects the 'graphics' capability (which is what mounts the Vulkan ICD) is a host-config question this catalog cannot answer. It is set below as a best-effort, and start.sh reports what it actually sees.

name: rigma-runpod

_field_notes.image: Build it with the Dockerfile beside this file. It MUST be pushed to a registry the pod can pull from (Docker Hub, GHCR, or Runpod's own) — Runpod pulls the image, it does not build it.
_field_notes.disk: 20 GB of container disk, the vendor's own value for this base. The base plus Rigma plus the pinned Vulkan engine (~30 MiB) is the bulk; the rest is headroom for Rigma's sessions/logs/rigma.db and for a model downloaded while the volume is still cold. Container disk is WIPED on pod stop.
_field_notes.ports: 11500/http is the port Runpod's proxy exposes (https://<pod-id>-11500.proxy.runpod.net) AND the port the UI now binds directly, because `rigma up --host 0.0.0.0` exists (commit in this branch). One port, not three: no socat, no separate UI port, no port left free for a collision that can no longer happen. 22/tcp is the SSH control channel. Ports are set at creation and cannot be added to a running pod without a reset (pod-workflows.md:19).
_field_notes.RIGMA_UI_PORT / RIGMA_HOST: The single public port and the interface to bind. rigma up --port P --host H puts the UI on H:P and the engine on 127.0.0.1:(P-1) — models.py:800 pins llama-server to loopback regardless, so only the UI is ever reachable off-box. Set RIGMA_HOST=127.0.0.1 only for in-pod debugging: the proxy then 502s, and start.sh says so.
_field_notes.RIGMA_RUNPOD_BACKEND: vulkan (default) | cpu | off. Since commit 634b1d4 Rigma skips backends with no pinned build by itself, so 'vulkan' is belt-and-braces plus the catch-all row for cards absent from gpus.json; 'cpu' is the deliberate CPU-only bench; 'off' leaves the packaged registry alone to reproduce the unshimmed choice. See the README's GPU backend matrix.
_field_notes.RIGMA_AUTO_CALIBRATE: Rigma's own variable (cli.py:2890-2891). "1" runs the one-time hardware sweep on first load of a model (minutes, and it relaunches the engine several times on port UI-1). "0" skips it. For a test bench the sweep is usually the point; set it to 0 for a fast, reproducible start.
_field_notes.HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET: runtime.py:376 sets this with setdefault() anyway; setting it explicitly is documentation, and it keeps the model download on HF's plain CDN path.
_field_notes.NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES: Needed for the default Vulkan lane: the NVIDIA Vulkan ICD (/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json) and libGLX_nvidia are only mounted into the container when the 'graphics' capability is enabled. NO stock Runpod template sets it (all 14 have env {}), so the platform is not doing it for you — but the catalog cannot show what the HOST injects either. UNVERIFIED: start.sh prints the ICD directory and Rigma's own probe result at boot, which is the real answer.
_field_notes.mounts: `persistent` only, because the template API refuses `network` (see _schema_provenance.mounts_shape). The stock templates declare path /workspace, size 20; 100 GB here because models are GB-scale. A NETWORK volume is still the durable option and the one to use for a real bench — it survives pod termination, while /workspace on a pod without one is container disk and is wiped (golden path 01, 'Models vanish after stop') — but it is attached at POD creation, not declared here. start.sh checks `stat -f` on /workspace and warns when it is not a network mount.
_field_notes.startSsh: true, and it matters: without SSH there is no way to exec into a pod whose UI fails to come up. The image's CMD chains the base image's /start.sh, which is what honours this.
_field_notes.startJupyter: false — Rigma serves its own UI, and Jupyter is another process to keep alive on a bench pod. Set true if you want the base image's notebook as a second way in.
_field_notes.allowedCudaVersions: The vendor's own list for this base image (runpod/pytorch:2.4.0-py3.11-cuda12.4.1-...). It constrains which hosts can run the pod; narrowing it to ["12.4"] reduces placement options for no benefit, since a 12.4 runtime works with newer drivers.
_field_notes.args: Empty. The container start command is the image's CMD (["/opt/rigma-runpod/start.sh"]), which itself chains the base image's /start.sh before exec'ing rigma. No catalog record sets args, so there is no evidence a template-level start command is even honoured — keeping it empty avoids the question.
_field_notes.public: false: this template references your own registry image, so there is no reason for it to be visible to other accounts. The stock templates are public: true.
_field_notes.category: NVIDIA. The stock CPU templates use "CPU"; this template needs a GPU for the Vulkan lane, and the CPU-only bench is a different deployment (RIGMA_RUNPOD_BACKEND=cpu on a GPU pod, or an Ubuntu CPU template).

_creation_calls.rest_v2_pod: POST https://api.runpod.io/v2/pods with Authorization: Bearer $RUNPOD_API_KEY and a body carrying image, disk, ports, env, mounts and gpuTypeIds (or templateId). This is the surface whose field names are verified above — the same key that listed the catalog authorizes it.
_creation_calls.runpodctl_pod_create: runpodctl pod create --name rigma --image <ns>/rigma-runpod:v1 --gpu-id "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090" --ports "11500/http,22/tcp" --env '{"RIGMA_RUNPOD_BACKEND":"vulkan"}' --container-disk-in-gb 20 --network-volume-id <vol-id> --volume-mount-path /workspace --data-center-ids <dc> --terminate-after <iso8601>   # runpodctl is NOT installed on this machine, so this line is from the golden paths (01-ollama-pod.md:84-92), not executed here
